title: Order jumps in Spectral Deferred Corrections: Theorem 2
author: Eugen Bronasco, Joscha Fregin, Daniel Ruprecht, Gilles Vilmart
work: Order jumps in Spectral Deferred Corrections
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 2 (source0.tex lines 2052--2062, source label thm:order_jump), the characterisation of when an iteration of a spectral deferred correction method that approximates a Runge--Kutta method of order p satisfying B(p), C(eta), D(zeta) with p = eta + zeta increases its iteration order by two, delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 2342--2367 (26 lines, one proof environment headed 'Proof of Theorem 2'; the article states the theorem in its section 5 and prints the proof in its section 6, so the proof is detached from the statement by the article's own arrangement and both spans are delivered). The theorem is the paper's central new result: it identifies exactly which effective error dynamics produce an order jump of two orders per sweep and under which stage conditions, and the proof is a complete research-level argument over Butcher trees: it reduces the claim to the equi-weight identity alpha^{K+1}(tau) = 1/tau! for all trees of size p_K+2, disposes of the branching case through the article's general-form lemma, and then treats the single-chain case by splitting on the two hypotheses and applying the article's eta-form lemma and the defining recursion for the weights omega. H2: a complete original main theorem with a fully written proof whose individual steps are Butcher-tree identities, not routine verifications.
